summary: Backend-only testing of the new HeartLink chat features (typing indicators + read receipts) on the preview URL. Created /app/backend/tests/test_chat_typing_read.py (15 pytest tests): 14 PASS, 1 FAIL by design documenting a security/validation gap. Verified end-to-end: signed up 2 TEST_ users -> mutual like -> real match -> sent messages via POST /api/messages -> GET /api/messages/{match_id} returns the new read/read_at fields (read_at=null initially, no _id leak) -> POST /api/messages/{match_id}/read?reader_id=... marks ONLY the reader's inbound messages read, persists read_at, is idempotent (2nd call count=0), returns 422 without reader_id -> POST /api/messages/{match_id}/typing?user_id=... returns 200 for both participants, honours is_typing=false, returns 404 for unknown match, 422 without user_id. WebSocket wss://.../api/ws/{user_id} verified with two live sockets: 'typing' event from user A is delivered to user B with correct match_id/user_id/is_typing; a message sent over WS reaches the receiver with read=false/read_at=null; 'mark_read' from B pushes a 'messages_read' event (match_id, read_by, read_at) to A and the read state is persisted in MongoDB (confirmed via GET). Frontend ChatPage.jsx WS contract (typing: {type,match_id,receiver_id,is_typing}; mark_read: {type,match_id}) matches the backend handler exactly. Test users were deleted after the run (verified 0 TEST_Chat users remain).

minor.issue: No match-membership / auth validation. Any caller passing an arbitrary user_id (not part of the match) gets 200 and, because the code does `if match.user1_id == user_id ... else other_user_id = match.user1_id`, the typing event is pushed to user1 with a spoofed user_id. An outsider can make either participant see 'X is typing...'. Should 403 when user_id is neither user1_id nor user2_id (test_typing_non_participant_is_rejected).
No auth and no match/participant validation (IDOR): any anonymous caller can mark someone else's messages read for any match_id. Unknown match_id silently returns 200 with count=0 instead of 404.

Sender notification uses `db.messages.find_one({match_id, receiver_id: reader_id})` (arbitrary/first doc) to derive sender_id. Works only for 1:1 chats; for any future group/multi-sender thread the messages_read event goes to the wrong user. Prefer using the match document participants or the distinct sender_ids of the updated messages.

user_id comes from the path with no token/auth, so any client can open a socket as any user, receive that user's messages/typing events and emit mark_read on their behalf. Also `message_data['receiver_id']` and `message_data['content']` are accessed without validation - a malformed frame raises KeyError inside the receive loop and kills the connection (only WebSocketDisconnect is caught, so the user is not marked offline on that path).

Both take user_id/reader_id as required QUERY params rather than a request body/auth context - inconsistent with the rest of the API and unused by the frontend (ChatPage sends typing/mark_read only over WebSocket), so these HTTP endpoints are effectively dead code today.

action_items: MEDIUM (security): validate match membership in POST /api/messages/{match_id}/typing (403 if user_id not in {user1_id,user2_id}) instead of defaulting to user1_id.
MEDIUM (security): validate that reader_id is a participant of match_id in POST /api/messages/{match_id}/read and return 404 for unknown match_id.
MEDIUM: wrap the WebSocket receive loop message parsing in try/except (KeyError/JSONDecodeError) so a malformed frame does not drop the socket without running the offline/disconnect cleanup.
LOW: derive the messages_read notification target from the match participants (or distinct sender_ids of updated messages) instead of an arbitrary find_one.
LOW: either wire ChatPage to the HTTP /typing and /read endpoints as a WS fallback, or drop them to avoid unauthenticated duplicate surface area.
critical_code_review_comments: /app/backend/server.py is now 4152 lines - the chat/typing/read handlers should move into a dedicated router module.

The mark-read update logic is duplicated verbatim in the HTTP /read endpoint and the WS 'mark_read' branch - extract a shared async helper (mark_match_read(match_id, reader_id)) so the two paths cannot drift.

GET /api/messages/{match_id} re-validates every doc through Message(**m); a doc missing a required field (legacy rows) will raise 500 - consider Message.model_validate with defaults or a projection-based response.
No auth dependency on any chat endpoint or on the WebSocket path; user identity is fully client-supplied.

success_rate.backend: 93% (14/15). All 6 requested features verified working; the single failure is an intentional defect-documenting test for missing match-membership validation on /typing.

seed_data_creation: Two temporary users TEST_Chat User1/User2 (@example.com, random suffix) + one real match and a handful of TEST_ messages. Users deleted in fixture teardown via DELETE /api/admin/user/{id}; verified /api/admin/all-users?search=TEST_Chat returns 0.
test_credentials: referraltest@heartlink.com / Test@123 valid. NOTE: /api/auth/login expects `email_or_phone`. Signup rejects .test TLD emails (email-validator blocks reserved TLDs) - use @example.com for seeded users.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run: cd /app/backend && python -m pytest tests/test_chat_typing_read.py -v -p no:randomly --asyncio-mode=auto  (pytest-asyncio 1.4.0 was installed by me; there is no pytest.ini in /app/backend so --asyncio-mode=auto is required). The suite self-provisions a matched pair of TEST_ users and cleans them up. Only TestTypingIndicator::test_typing_non_participant_is_rejected should fail until membership validation is added. WebSocket testing works over wss://<REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL host>/api/ws/{user_id} with the `websockets` package (15.0.1). Frontend ChatPage typing/read UI was NOT exercised in the browser this iteration.
rca_of_the_issue: No functional defect found in the new typing/read-receipt features - both HTTP endpoints, the Message.read_at schema field, and both WebSocket branches behave as specified and persist correctly. The only real gap is authorization/validation: /typing computes the notification target with an if/else on user1_id, so an unknown user_id falls through to user1_id (spoofable typing events), and /read plus the WS handler trust a fully client-supplied identity.
